title: Route & Model Performance Riverboard - Compact distribution + token-flow widgets
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design a compact, embeddable ‘Riverboard’ for per-route and per-model performance that combines latency distributions, throughput lanes, and token-flow micro-watersheds. Goal: Surface key SLO signals at a glance for Console cards and the route inspector panel without overwhelming engineers with full charts. Emphasis on percentile overlays, bucketed latency bands, token ingress/egress visualization, and a small multiple layout for model variants.
acceptance_criteria: Responsive card-size layout available at 320px, 480px, 720px widths
Latency distribution shows p50/p90/p99 and shaded bucket bands
Throughput lane includes per-minute QPS sparkline + burst indicator
Token-flow waterfall supports prefix vs generation split and cumulative token cost
Accessible color contrast and tooltips for each micro-widget
Prototype linked and validated with two ENG and one PM reviewer
tasks: Finalize color palette and token-cost microglyphs (design)
Define latency bucket boundaries and labeling copy (pm + eng)
Implement accessible tooltip patterns and keyboard focus states (eng)
Add canary variant comparison mode to prototype (design)
Create e2e QA checklist for rendering under low-bandwidth conditions
decisions: Use bucketed latency bands instead of full violin plots to reduce ink and cognitive load
Show cumulative token cost as a subtle top overlay (instead of a separate chart) to conserve vertical space
Combine prefix vs generated token split into a stacked micro-waterfall with hover breakdowns
Default to p90 as the emphasized percentile in the compact view with option to expand to p99
tradeoffs: Precision vs density: bucketed bands lose per-request scatter but dramatically reduce visual noise in small cards
Interactivity vs performance: removing heavy SVG microtraces improves render time but limits advanced brushing on tiny cards
Single-card information density risks cognitive overload; mitigated by progressive disclosure on hover/expand
review_feedback: ENG (Lina Torres): prefer 6 buckets aligned to runtime kernel perf buckets to aid cross-team debugging
PM (Harold Kim): add explicit cost-per-1k-tokens annotation for quick economics checks
QA (Rafael Ortiz): ensure token waterfall flips for RTL locales and validate tooltip placement on small viewports
Design review (Maya Brooks): color contrast for p99 overlay needs + WCAG AA check; suggested darker outline
followups: ENG-18822: expose bucket boundaries via API for backend alignment
PM-4421: confirm default percentile for SLO alerts in product policy
DES-62900: create expanded full-size chart variant and transition animation spec
blockers: Backend endpoint for per-minute token breakdown currently returns samples only; needs aggregation support
Runtime team to confirm kernel-aligned latency bucket definitions before QA
notes: Prototype includes a compact expand animation where the riverboard card grows into the full route inspector with preserved zoom. We trialed three micro-widget orders — latency-first performed best in a lab usability test (n=8 engineers). Quantitative A/B suggested faster time-to-insight for error triage by ~17% vs baseline compact sparklines.
